memory_update.text: TSEM should be tracked as the underfollowed US-listed SiPho foundry-capacity candidate for the optical interconnect node.
FN should be tracked as a second-order optical manufacturing / advanced optical packaging capacity candidate, with customer concentration and cleanroom utilization as key follow-up variables.

The likely chokepoint stack is not only optical modules; it may sit in InP/GaAs laser capacity, SiPho foundry capacity, high-speed analog signal-integrity components, precision optical packaging, and compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools.

Aixtron appears to be one of the cleanest pure tool-layer exposures but is not a clean US-exchange-listed candidate; keep it as a non-US/OTC context anchor and use it to identify US-listed customers or adjacent equipment suppliers.
SMTC and MTSI were not included due to the four-candidate cap, but both should be revisited in a signal-integrity sub-pass for TIAs, laser drivers, retimers, and 1.6T/3.2T optical module components.

node: Optical interconnect, lasers, silicon photonics, and compound-semiconductor epitaxy tools
summary: Expanded the universe for the optical interconnect / laser / silicon-photonics / compound-semiconductor tool node with a two-lane funnel. Reference anchors are the obvious optical component and manufacturing beneficiaries, but the underfollowed lane points toward silicon-photonics foundry capacity, InP/GaAs laser supply, optical-module manufacturing capacity, and signal-integrity components. The cleanest US-exchange-listed candidates found in this pass are TSEM, LITE, COHR, and FN. Aixtron remains a highly relevant non-US/OTC ADR equipment-context name, but it is excluded from the candidate limit because the task prioritizes US-listed companies.
